findings.title: 3 image pair(s) leak between train and val
findings.detail: The validation split contains content the model trained on. Every metric computed against it is optimistic by an unknown margin, so it cannot be used to compare checkpoints or to decide the model is ready to ship. Re-split before doing anything else - fixing this after training means retraining.

findings.title: 20 box(es) fall outside the normalised [0,1] range
findings.detail: Coordinates outside [0,1] are clipped or rejected depending on the loader. Where they are clipped the box silently changes shape, so the model is trained against a target the annotator never drew.

findings.title: 2 box(es) use a class id that does not exist
findings.detail: An id at or above nc indexes past the model's classification head. Ultralytics raises on this during dataset verification; a hand-rolled loader will index out of bounds mid-epoch.
evidence: train/000000179265 line 1: class id 13 but data.yaml defines 12 classes (0..11)
train/000000479030 line 1: class id 15 but data.yaml defines 12 classes (0..11)

findings.title: 2 image(s) cannot be decoded
findings.detail: A corrupt image aborts the epoch in most training loops, or is skipped with a warning that is easy to miss in a long log.
evidence: train/000000336232: OSError: image file is truncated (40 bytes not processed)
train/000000376307: OSError: image file is truncated (42 bytes not processed)

findings.title: 2 box(es) have zero or negative width/height
findings.detail: A zero-area box produces a NaN in most IoU implementations, which propagates into the loss and ends the run.

findings.title: 2 file(s) hold pixel coordinates instead of normalised fractions
findings.detail: The values are bounded by the image dimensions rather than by 1.0, so this is an export that skipped the divide-by-width/height step. Training on it produces boxes that collapse to the top-left corner.

findings.title: 2 label row(s) are not parseable
findings.detail: A YOLO row must be `class_id xc yc w h`. Rows that are not will raise during dataset scanning or be skipped silently depending on the loader version.

findings.title: 3 box(es) are listed more than once in the same file
findings.detail: Duplicated boxes double-count in the loss and break the one-target-per-object assumption used by NMS-free matchers.

findings.title: 3 image(s) have no label file
findings.detail: Ultralytics treats an image with no .txt as a pure background image. If these are actually unlabelled foreground images the model is being explicitly taught that the objects in them are background, which suppresses recall for those classes.

findings.title: 3 box(es) are too small to survive the dataloader
findings.detail: Boxes with a normalised side below 0.003 are dropped during letterboxing. They inflate the apparent annotation count while contributing nothing, which makes per-class coverage look better than it is.
